# FDG7044

> DO use `value` for the name of the implicit value parameter of property setters.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.3.4 ArgumentException, ArgumentNullException, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG7044
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

Message: Name the parameter 'value' instead of '{0}' in an argument exception thrown by a setter

FDG7044 reports a constant passed to the paramName parameter of an argument exception (a type derived from System.ArgumentException) created in a property or indexer setter or init accessor, when it is neither "value" nor a parameter of the indexer. CA2208 accepts the property's own name there (probe with SDK 10.0.402), so it is not mapped. A paramName that is not a constant, and throw helpers called from the setter, are not seen, so coverage is partial. There is no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public FileAttributes Attributes {
   set {
      if(value==null){
        throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(value),...);
      }
   }
}
```

> **Jeffrey Richter:** It is very unusual to find code that catches any of these argument exceptions. When one of these exceptions is thrown, you almost always want the application to die. Then look at the exception stack trace, fix your source code so that you are passing the right argument, recompile the code, and retest.

> **Jason Clark:** Jeffrey is absolutely correct here. And it is the infrequency with which these exception types are caught that makes them safe to broadly reuse for throwing in your code.
